# The release tag grammar, as one corpus for every reader that holds a copy of
# it. Each line is a verdict and a tag: `canonical` is a tag the release channel
# may offer, `refused` is one it never does, however high it ranks.
#
# A refused tag here passes ValidTag and carries a high version on purpose, so a
# reader that loses the grammar check picks it and the test goes red. rc.0 stays
# canonical: a release tool may refuse to cut it, but a reader takes it.

canonical v0.0.0
canonical v0.3.0
canonical v0.3.0-rc.0
canonical v0.3.0-rc.1
canonical v0.3.0-rc.9
canonical v0.3.0-rc.10
canonical v0.3.0-rc.9999
canonical v10.20.30
canonical v999999999.999999999.999999999

# Not three plain numeric fields behind a lowercase v.
refused 9.0.0
refused V9.0.0
refused v9.0
refused v9.0.0.0
refused v09.0.0
refused v9.00.0
refused v9.0.00
refused v1000000000.0.0

# A candidate suffix in any other spelling.
refused v9.0.0-rc
refused v9.0.0-rc.
refused v9.0.0-rc1
refused v9.0.0-RC.1
refused v9.0.0-rc.01
refused v9.0.0-rc.10000
refused v9.0.0-rc.1.2
refused v9.0.0-rc.1+build.5

# Another prerelease name, and build metadata.
refused v9.0.0-alpha
refused v9.0.0-beta.1
refused v9.0.0+build.5

# A development build, a modified tree, and Go pseudo-versions.
refused dev
refused v9.0.0-dev
refused v9.0.0-dirty
refused v9.0.0.dirty
refused v9.0.0+dirty
refused v0.0.0-20261015120000-0123456789ab
refused v9.0.1-0.20261015120000-0123456789ab
refused v9.0.1-rc.1.0.20261015120000-0123456789ab
